commits.message:
[vpsAdminOS] mm: expose proactive swap via virtual swap views v11

Host-managed proactive reclaim must not consume the virtual swap capacity
reserved for a container's own memory policy. Preserve the reclaim origin
of each swap entry and expose proactive usage independently of normal
virtual capacity through the vpsAdminOS memory and swap views.

Record proactive identity alongside the existing swap-cgroup IDs, account
it to the appropriate memcg hierarchy, and uncharge it when entries are
released. Exclude proactive usage from normal virtual used capacity and
report the additional virtual-system pool consistently in /proc/swaps,
/proc/meminfo and sysinfo(), including zero normal-capacity configurations.
These synthetic views and the host-managed reclaim admission policy are
intentional vpsAdminOS behavior, not a change to ordinary upstream swap.

Allocate the identity bitmap with kvcalloc() using an unsigned-long bit
count. One bit per swap page becomes several MiB for a large swap device;
bitmap_zalloc() requires physically contiguous kmalloc memory and can
request an unsupported allocation order despite abundant free RAM. Allow
vmalloc fallback and pair it with kvfree() on setup failure and swapoff.
The bitmap is CPU-addressed metadata and has no physical-contiguity
requirement. Do not change swap limits, disable accounting or hide errors.

Keep the 6.12 paged swap-cgroup map and its locking/accounting interfaces.
The existing view-accounting completion belongs to this same feature and
is folded here; unrelated downstream changes are replayed unchanged.
Original implementation and accounting: Pavel Snajdr, April 2026.

Development history:
Initial: introduced proactive entry identity and virtual swap reporting,
then completed separation of normal and proactive used capacity.
v11: combine those coupled changes and correct large-bitmap allocation
and both release paths. The version continues the proactive-reclaim
feature family's v10 development history on the 6.18 line; it does not
claim that 6.18-only implementation changes were backported to 6.12.

Validation: the allocation delta passes git diff --check and checkpatch
with no errors or warnings. Normal OS integration adds parallel large-
swap activation/deactivation cases for both kernel series and cgroup
modes. Runtime results are recorded separately, not claimed here.
mm/damon: add per-node reclaim scope support
mm/damon: fix damon_reclaim scope updates from sysfs

mm: memcg: fix NULL deref in __invalidate_reclaim_iterators

invalidate_reclaim_iterators() walks the parent chain via
parent_mem_cgroup() and calls __invalidate_reclaim_iterators() on
each ancestor to clear its reclaim iterator position.  Since commit
ded4d207a320 ("cgroup: split cgroup_destroy_wq into 3 workqueues"),
the offline, release, and free stages of cgroup destruction run on
separate workqueues, making it possible for an ancestor memcg to be
freed via css_free_rwork_fn() on cgroup_free_wq while a child's
css_release_work_fn() on cgroup_release_wq is still traversing the
parent chain.

The crash manifests as:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 00000000000001a0
  RIP: 0010:__invalidate_reclaim_iterators+0x42/0x90

where from->nodeinfo[nid] is NULL because the ancestor memcg has
already been deallocated.

Fix this with two complementary changes:

1) Hold rcu_read_lock() around the ancestor walk.  css_free_rwork_fn()
   is queued via queue_rcu_work() so it cannot run while an RCU reader
   is active, preventing ancestors from being freed during the walk.

2) Add a defensive NULL check on from->nodeinfo[nid] to handle any
   remaining edge case where the per-node data is absent.

Reported-by: vpsAdminOS node2 staging crash 2026-05-08
Signed-off-by: Pavel Snajdr <snajpa@snajpa.net>

vpsadminos: fix memcg CSS ref ownership in memory views

The 6.12.87 crash in flush_memcg_stats_dwork faulted in
mem_cgroup_css_rstat_flush() while reading
parent->nodeinfo[0]->lruvec_stats. A live child memcg should make that
state impossible: cgroup core stores css->parent and takes a reference to
it in init_and_link_css(), so the parent CSS and its memcg per-node state
must outlive the child CSS. The NULL parent->nodeinfo[] therefore was not
the root cause; it was fallout from earlier CSS refcount corruption.

The vpsAdminOS memory virtualization helper could corrupt that lifetime.
get_current_most_limited_memcg() selected a memcg under RCU, called
css_tryget(), but only WARNed on failure and returned the pointer anyway.
Callers then used it as refcounted and later mem_cgroup_put() it, which
can drop a reference that was never acquired.

The /proc/swaps virtual path had an independent imbalance. swaps_open()
took a memcg reference and passed it as single_open() private data, but
fake_swap_show() dropped the reference. single_open() keeps the private
pointer for the file lifetime, so a seek/read can call show again and put
the same memcg twice, while an open that is never read leaks it.

Fix the helper by pinning current's memory css with task_get_css() before
walking the hierarchy. While that ref is held, ancestors are stable
through the css parent-reference chain, so taking a reference on the
selected ancestor with css_get() is valid. Fix /proc/swaps by owning the
memcg reference for the seq file lifetime: put it on open failure or
release, not from show().

Fixes: 6faa96270cfc ("[vpsAdminOS] Common functions")
Fixes: 92726ab7d1f5 ("[vpsAdminOS] Virtualize meminfo and swaps v4")
Signed-off-by: Pavel Snajdr <snajpa@snajpa.net>

sched: intersect vpsadminos fake affinity masks

The vpsAdminOS cgroup-namespace sched_setaffinity() path rejected any
requested mask that was not a strict subset of the fake online CPU mask.
That is stricter than the regular scheduler path, which intersects the
requested mask with the allowed cpuset and only fails when the result is
empty.

crun 1.27 resets inherited CPU affinity by setting a full userspace
cpu_set_t mask. In a container with a CPU quota, that reaches this fake
CPU path as an oversized but intersecting mask and fails with EINVAL,
which prevents CPU-limited nested Podman containers from starting.

Intersect the requested mask with the fake online mask before storing it.
This keeps out-of-range-only masks invalid while accepting broad masks
that include at least one visible CPU.

Signed-off-by: Jakub Skokan <jakub.skokan@havefun.cz>
vpsadminos: tolerate missing early memcg CSS

[vpsAdminOS] NFS: tolerate a cold NLM client during sysfs shutdown

An NFSv3 mount allocates an nlm_host before its first remote lock, but
nlm_host.h_rpcclnt is still NULL until then. The server shutdown attribute
passes that pointer to shutdown_client(), which otherwise dereferences it
unconditionally. Cancellation can therefore crash the host even when the
mount has never used NLM.

There are no RPC tasks to cancel when the client has not been allocated.
Leave the server's terminal state handling unchanged and skip only the
absent RPC client.

Carry the existing 6.12.109 OS compatibility repair in the downstream
source so upgrading the stable kernel retains the same NULL-safe behavior.
The version-scoped OS patch remains in place for the retained older pin.

Signed-off-by: Pavel Snajdr <snajpa@snajpa.net>
